exposure: Midwife-led telephone psycho-education intervention for childbirth fear
cohort: Pregnant women in their second trimester with high childbirth fear scores (Wijma Delivery Expectancy / Experience Questionnaire (W-DEQ) >= 66) were recruited for this multi-site study.
finding: Women receiving the antenatal midwife-led psycho-education intervention for childbirth fear were less likely to experience distressing flashbacks of birth, preferred a normal birth in a future pregnancy, and showed a reduction in overall caesarean section rates compared to controls.
mod_finding: The intervention group had a clinically meaningful but not statistically significant reduction in overall caesarean section (34% vs 42%) and emergency caesarean section rates (18% vs 25%).
